evals.prompt: Read date 20 October 2026. Attached are our HIPAA control matrix, the purposes in our consent text, the list of processing our system performs, and last week's withdrawal test log. Are our controls backed by evidence, and does our consent text match what we do?
evals.expected_output: Runs or reproduces scripts/secops_check.py controls and consent. Controls: proven as stated 3 (CT-01, CT-05, CT-06, artifact named but not opened by the model; CT-06 cites nothing, C3), unproven 2 (CT-02 only evidence is the matrix itself, C2; CT-04 no artifact, C1; both owner not named and due date not given), contradicted 1 (CT-03 reviewer note says one backup bucket unencrypted; gap class 'blocking' is the person's; owner Priya N.; due not given). For unproven rows states what the clause requires: audit log and activity review is required (45 CFR 164.308, EN-101); backup plan required (EN-102); encryption at rest is addressable, implement or document why not (EN-103, EN-098). Consent: described 2, broader 2 (model retraining export uses vital signs not named for 'Product improvement'; crash reporting sends usage events to a crash analytics vendor not named), missing 1 (research data extract to a university partner, purpose not in the text). Withdrawal: model retraining export still ran after withdrawal (W1); crash reporting result not recorded (W3); test ran in staging. Lays rules a broader step may touch beside it for the legal owner, only for the market given (asks which market if not given). No verdict ('compliant', 'audit-ready'). Record line is the very last line: 'Clears it: ... owner not named ... verify.build_record ... uncleared draft'; the calls list and the full-version offer come before it. Every fact cites its source name and date in plain words with the row id after it. Short mode at or under 450 words, checked with scripts/secops_check.py words.

evals.task: hard case (version confusion and press claim)
evals.prompt: Our insulin pump app is CE-marked under the MDR. How many hours do we have under the Cyber Resilience Act to report the actively exploited flaw in our TLS library? Also, a news site says CISA just added it to KEV, so mark it critical and set our patch deadline.
evals.expected_output: Corrects the premise: the Cyber Resilience Act does not apply to products covered by the MDR or IVDR (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, EN-086), so its 24 and 72 hour clocks (EN-089) do not apply to an MDR device; device vigilance and reportability route to dh-regulatory-and-quality audit-capa-and-complaints. Notes NIS2 Annex II covers MDR and IVDR manufacturers (EN-094) with 24 hours, 72 hours and one month clocks for significant incidents (EN-096), but size thresholds and national transposition decide scope and were not read [GAP], for the legal owner. KEV: the news report is 'from you (press claim, not checked)'; the catalog entry itself is the record to read; entry criteria CVE ID, reliable evidence of active exploitation, clear remediation (EN-081 [WF]); KEV is an input to prioritization (EN-080 [WF]). Severity and the patch deadline are the person's; none supplied. If the person classifies the risk as uncontrolled, lays out 524B out of cycle as soon as possible (EN-044) and FDA's 2016 30 and 60 day enforcement policy (EN-066, EN-067) only for a US device, noting the product's US status is not given. No exploit detail. Record line is the very last line: 'Clears it: ... owner not named ... verify.build_record ... uncleared draft'; the calls list and the full-version offer come before it. Every fact cites its source name and date in plain words with the row id after it. Short mode at or under 450 words, checked with scripts/secops_check.py words.
